option.counterfactual: There is a pure k-decomposable complex that cannot be completed on its existing vertex set while keeping every intermediate complex k-decomposable, so b(d,k) is positive for some parameters.
option.approach: Investigate whether one new vertex always removes the obstruction by supplying missing lower-dimensional faces through mixed facets. Combine that construction with the counterexample to establish an exact value of one in a parameter range.

options.approach: Audit the claimed multiple-vertex obstruction directly, checking the first-exit argument against facets containing auxiliary vertices. Look for boundary faces introduced by earlier mixed facets that the obstruction overlooks.

options.approach: Revisit completion along a decomposition tree, assigning auxiliary vertices to the vertices of each shedding face. Try to prove that a buffer of k-1 vertices guarantees purity and enough capacity in every recursive target.
